title: A pigment layer over a tunable Bragg reflector: how much colour is reachable, and which layer stops it
kind: optical model (transfer-matrix multilayer + areal pigment mixing + CIE colorimetry)
headline: Freezing the iridophore stack removes 88% of the achievable gamut, so the multilayer is what produces the colour; but widening its measured 425-675 nm tuning range buys 1%, whereas raising the reflectin refractive index from the live-cell mean 1.405 to the measured maximum 1.44 buys 68% and a nearly transparent retracted state buys 61%. The limit is refractive-index contrast and the chromatophore's retraction floor, not tuning range. Removing the yellow pigment class makes the gamut BIGGER, because at the only sourced expansion ratio a retracted chromatophore still covers 52% of the skin.

model.description: Seawater over three independently driven ommochrome pigment classes (areal coverage each, double-pass absorbers), over an N-pair reflectin/inter-lamellar Bragg stack computed by transfer matrix at normal incidence, over a switchable broadband leucophore backing. Chromaticity in CIE 1976 u'v' under CIE D65 and the CIE 1931 2-degree observer; gamut is the convex-hull area of the achievable u'v' set.
state_variables: areal coverage of each of three pigment classes, in [f_retracted, f_expanded]
Bragg peak wavelength (set by scaling the layer pair at fixed ratio)
equations: stack: characteristic-matrix product over N (high, low) pairs at normal incidence
first-order Bragg peak: lambda = 2 (n_H d_H + n_L d_L)
pigment: T(lambda) = 10^(-OD * a(lambda)), a a long-pass sigmoid
areal mixing, double pass: R = R_under * prod_k (f_k T_k^2 + 1 - f_k)
backing: R_under = R_bragg + (1 - R_bragg)^2 * R_backing (one bounce)
XYZ = k * integral CMF(lambda) * E(lambda) * R(lambda) d lambda

parameters.name: n_low
parameters.source: Inter-lamellar space. Ghoshal A, DeMartini DG, Eck E, Morse DE 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, PMID 23740489 (read: full text via PMC) set n_L = 1.34 to match the refractive index of the artificial-seawater bath, which they measured with a refractometer, because the spaces are continuous with it.

parameters.name: n_high
parameters.source: Reflectin-filled lamellae in LIVE cells: 1.405 +/- 0.012, range 1.38-1.44, rarely to 1.48. Ghoshal A, DeMartini DG, Eck E, Morse DE 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, PMID 23740489 (read: full text via PMC). Ghoshal A et al. 2014, J R Soc Interface 11:20140106, PMID 24694894 (read: abstract) measured the condensed lamellae directly at about 1.44 by index matching.

parameters.name: n_medium
parameters.source: Incident medium taken as the same seawater index. Not separately measured for the skin surface, which carries mucus and epidermis.

parameters.name: n_pairs
parameters.source: Eight or nine pairs contribute in live cells; six or seven in chemically fixed ones. Ghoshal A, DeMartini DG, Eck E, Morse DE 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, PMID 23740489 (read: full text via PMC).

parameters.name: d_high_live
parameters.source: 120 +/- 15 nm, live cells, table 1. Ghoshal A, DeMartini DG, Eck E, Morse DE 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, PMID 23740489 (read: full text via PMC).

parameters.name: d_low_live
parameters.source: 95 +/- 14 nm, live cells, table 1. Ghoshal A, DeMartini DG, Eck E, Morse DE 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, PMID 23740489 (read: full text via PMC).

parameters.name: lambda_tuning_range
parameters.source: Measured peak tuning, 675 nm (red) to 425 nm (blue). Ghoshal A, DeMartini DG, Eck E, Morse DE 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, PMID 23740489 (read: full text via PMC).

parameters.name: thickness_ratio
parameters.source: Held constant while scaling the pair to a target peak. The Bragg condition is one equation in two thicknesses; the live-cell mean ratio is used to close it. The paper reports a weak positive correlation (Pearson R ~ 0.59) of BOTH thicknesses with peak wavelength, which is consistent with scaling at fixed ratio but does not establish it.

parameters.name: pigment_edge_nm
parameters.source: Long-pass absorption edges of the three ommochrome classes. NO measured cephalopod ommochrome absorption spectrum was found. Reiter S, Laurent G et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, PMID 30333578 (read: full text) measured chromatophore transmission spectra, found them bimodal at 615 nm, and localised xanthommatin to the light class, which fixes the ORDER yellow < red < brown and the long-pass SHAPE. The three numbers are chosen by hand inside that ordering.

parameters.name: pigment_width_nm
parameters.source: Sharpness of each absorption edge. No measurement; chosen by hand.

parameters.name: pigment_od
parameters.source: Peak optical density of one expanded pigment disc. No measurement.

parameters.name: area_ratio
parameters.source: +155.06% mean chromatophore surface area on expansion. Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: abstract here; the actuator study read the full text). This is a startle response, not a measured maximum.

parameters.name: coverage_full
parameters.source: Areal coverage with every chromatophore of a class expanded. Not measured. The retracted coverage is then DERIVED from the sourced area ratio rather than assumed separately, and comes out at 0.52.

parameters.name: r_leucophore
parameters.source: Broadband diffuse reflectance of the leucophore layer. Not measured in any source read; leucophores are described as broadband scatterers.

parameters.name: r_dermis
parameters.source: Reflectance of the tissue below the stack when no leucophore is present.

parameters.name: illuminant
parameters.source: CIE standard illuminant D65, 1 nm, from the CVRL database (cvrl.ioo.ucl.ac.uk/database/data/cie/Illuminantd65.csv, retrieved 2026-11-02). NOT a measured underwater spectrum; see limitations.

parameters.name: observer
parameters.source: CIE 1931 2-degree colour-matching functions, 1 nm, from the CVRL database (ciexyz31_1.csv, retrieved 2026-11-02). A HUMAN observer; cephalopods are colour-blind and their fish predators are not human.

parameters.name: peak_sampling_step
parameters.source: Sampling step of the Bragg peak across whatever tuning range an arm uses. Held constant so arms differ in coverage, not in sampling.

model.parameter_note: `sourced` means the number appears in a paper we read, measured in the thing being modelled. A value measured in another tissue or another species is `assumed`, with the proxy named in `source`.

derived.note_on_coverage: f_expanded is assumed at 0.85; f_retracted is then DERIVED from the sourced 2.5506x area ratio and comes out at 0.52. The model therefore has no transparent state, and that is a consequence of the only sourced expansion number rather than a choice.

bragg_fixed_at_live_mean.label: iridophore held at the live-cell mean stack

wider_area_ratio_10x.label: WIDENING: chromatophore area ratio 10x, not the measured 2.55x

wider_bragg_380_780.label: WIDENING: Bragg tuning over the whole visible band

higher_n_high_1p44.label: WIDENING: n_H at the measured maximum 1.44, not the mean 1.405

wider_area_ratio_50x.label: WIDENING: chromatophore area ratio 50x, i.e. a retracted state that is nearly transparent

wider_bragg_and_n_high.label: WIDENING: both optical dials at once

sweep_note: Each sweep moves ONE dial and recomputes the whole achievable set. The pair-count and refractive-index sweeps are the quantitative form of the ablation's claim that index contrast, not tuning range, is the limit; the area-ratio sweep shows what a chromatophore with a transparent off-state would be worth. The live animal sits at 8-9 pairs, n_H = 1.405 and an area ratio of 2.55, all three of which are measured.

which_layer_limits.field_note: `largest_gain_when_widened` can name a combination arm, which is not a dial anyone could turn on its own. The single-dial winner is reported separately, and it is the number quoted in the headline.
which_layer_limits.answer: Two different questions have two different answers, and conflating them is the easy mistake. The layer that PROVIDES the gamut is the iridophore stack: freeze it and 88% of the chromaticity area goes. The layer that LIMITS the gamut is not the same one. Widening the stack's tuning range beyond the measured 425-675 nm gains 1%, because that range already spans the visually useful band. What gains is refractive-index contrast (n_H 1.405 -> 1.44, the measured maximum: +68%) and chromatophore retraction (area ratio 2.55 -> 50, i.e. a retracted state that gets out of the way: +61%). Both are measured quantities that the animal is already at the edge of, so neither is a free lunch; the engineering reading is that a synthetic version should spend its effort on index contrast in the reflector and on a pigment actuator with a genuinely transparent off-state, and not on a wider tunable range.

controls.name: illuminant_white_point
controls.asks: does a perfect diffuse white under the loaded D65 and CIE 1931 2-degree CMFs land on the published D65 chromaticity?
controls.note: This is the control for the data files, not for the model. It is the positive control that makes the gamut numbers below readable: a mis-parsed CMF table and a correct one both produce a gamut.

controls.name: tmm_vs_quarter_wave_closed_form
controls.asks: does the transfer matrix reproduce the textbook quarter-wave reflectance at the design wavelength?
controls.note: This control failed on its first run with a worst error of 0.033, and reading it showed the error was in the CLOSED FORM, not in the transfer matrix: the admittance had been written as (n_H/n_L)^2N * n_H^2/(n_in n_L) instead of (n_H/n_L)^2N * n_out. The wrong side is recorded because a control that is itself wrong is the failure mode this check exists to make visible.

controls.name: index_matched_stack_is_dark
controls.asks: with the two indices equal, does the stack reflect nothing?
controls.threshold: index-matched max R < 1e-6 while the real stack is > 0.1
controls.note: The positive arm is shipped beside the negative one: a transfer matrix that silently returned zero would pass the negative arm alone.

controls.name: reproduce_published_tuning
controls.asks: do the paper's quoted endpoint thicknesses reproduce its quoted 425-675 nm tuning range?
controls.finding: FAILS, and the failure is in the source rather than in this model. Ghoshal 2013's abstract and conclusion give the tuning excursion as 'ca 150 to 80 nm' for the high-index lamellae and 'ca 120 to 50 nm' for the inter-lamellar spaces, for a measured peak moving 675 -> 425 nm. Taking those four numbers literally with the paper's own n_L = 1.34 and mean n_H = 1.405, the first-order Bragg condition gives 743 nm and 359 nm. No constant pair of indices satisfies both endpoints: matching 675 nm at d_H = 150 needs n_L = 1.06, and matching 425 nm at d_H = 80 needs n_L = 2.0. The quoted excursions are evidently rounded ('ca'). We therefore drive the model from the MEASURED peak range 425-675 nm and solve for thicknesses at the measured live-cell thickness ratio, rather than from the quoted endpoint dimensions. The live-cell averages are consistent: d_H = 120, d_L = 95 give 592 nm, a green, inside the range.

limitations: The illuminant is CIE D65, not a measured underwater downwelling spectrum. We did not find one we could read, and did not invent one. Seawater attenuates red strongly with depth, so the real gamut of a cephalopod in its own light field is smaller than this and shifted blue-green; we do not estimate by how much.

The observer is the CIE 1931 2-degree HUMAN observer. Cephalopods are colour-blind (one visual pigment in the species studied) and the predators they hide from are fish, often tetrachromatic. A gamut area in human u'v' is a convenient common currency, not the quantity that matters to either animal.

No measured absorption spectrum for a cephalopod ommochrome was found, so all nine pigment numbers (three edges, three widths, three optical densities) are assumed. The ORDER of the classes and the long-pass SHAPE are supported by Reiter et al. 2018's measured transmission spectra and xanthommatin localisation; the positions are not.

The stack is computed at normal incidence only. Real iridophore reflectance is strongly angle-dependent and the lamellae are not parallel to the skin surface, so an off-axis observer sees a different colour. This model cannot say anything about the angular gamut.

Scattering is ignored. The leucophore is a diffuse backing with a single number; pigment granules are treated as a pure absorber with no surface reflection, so the pigment can only darken and filter, never add a specular highlight.
The one-bounce addition of the backing beneath the stack is an approximation; a full multiple-scattering treatment would raise the reflectance of the leucophore-on states somewhat.

The Bragg peak is placed by holding the live-cell thickness RATIO constant and scaling the pair. The source reports both thicknesses correlating with peak wavelength, which is consistent with that but does not establish it; the animal may move the two thicknesses independently, which would make the reachable set larger than modelled.

Iridophores and chromatophores run at timescales two orders of magnitude apart (chromatophore expansion ~0.2 s; neurally evoked iridophore colour shift 17 s and brightness 32 s, Wardill et al. 2012). This model is steady-state and says nothing about what gamut is reachable QUICKLY.
